items.headline: Houthi ballistic-missile strike kills 50+ at Yemen camp; Saudi postpones 'Davos in the Desert' to 2027
bullets: Three Houthi ballistic missiles hit the al-Alam training camp (Ahmed al-Sulaimani Centre) in Shabwa province Monday — at least 53 security recruits killed, 200+ wounded per local authorities (Reuters' first wire said 18 before the toll rose; AP/BBC/PBS carry 53). Largest single loss of life since Yemen's civil war reignited in September. Houthi spokesman acknowledged the strike, calling the camp a 'Saudi enemy' concentration.

Saudi Arabia postponed its flagship Future Investment Initiative ('Davos in the Desert', scheduled Oct 26–29) to 2027 — organizers confirmed Monday (Reuters). Biggest investor-facing casualty of the escalation so far, after Houthi strikes on Riyadh's airport and Aramco HQ this month.

Market read: the escalation stays inside the Iran-war oil arc already in the feed — no contradiction with oil's soft Monday (Brent -1.9%, WTI -1.6% in Monday wraps): that move was the Friday EO waiver repricing, not this news.
